prompt: I need a tight upper bound on the number of comparisons merge sort makes on n elements, with a proof I can put in my thesis.

replies.report: Bound: C(n) <= n*ceil(log2 n) - 2^ceil(log2 n) + 1, tight for every n. Proof by strong induction on n: a merge of sizes a and b uses at most a+b-1 comparisons, and the recurrence C(n) = C(ceil(n/2)) + C(floor(n/2)) + n - 1 solves to the bound (full proof follows) ...

arguments.brief:
## Goal
Give the tight worst-case upper bound on the number of comparisons top-down merge sort makes on n elements, with a rigorous proof suitable for a thesis.

## Context
Standard top-down merge sort splitting into ceil(n/2) and floor(n/2); a merge of sizes a and b uses at most a+b-1 comparisons.

## Constraints
Answer in one reply; no tools. Exact bound, not just big-O.

## Acceptance
- A closed-form bound valid for every n >= 1, shown tight.
- A complete proof (induction on n) with every step justified.

## Output format
The bound on one line, then the proof in LaTeX-friendly prose.

reference.content: Merge sort makes at most n*ceil(log2 n) - 2^ceil(log2 n) + 1 comparisons, and this is tight. Proof: by strong induction on n using C(n) = C(ceil(n/2)) + C(floor(n/2)) + n - 1 ...
